precursor_10_15.scope: The preceding rule pairs inputs in order. Its ḍha and short aṭac are prior-rule labels; in this print the fish is maccha. No transfer from that prior-rule assignment to the extension.

word_readings.root: mā māne or māṅ māne śabde ca
word_readings.apparatus_or_limit: Witness ka has additional verbal paraphrases and both agent and object readings.
Witness ka instead reads dhyānaḥ. The main stem and its sense must not be conflated with the five-pāda dhyātva thought.
The five-pāda comparison already has an inflection table for the rice word.
The source puts the result in the masculine singular.
The object and agent are alternative derivational explanations of the printed word.
Witness ka reads prasannam instead of the main gloss āsanam.

extension_10_16.affix_evidence: The extension states that the affixes beginning with itva are seen on other roots and supplies examples. It does not give a one-to-one suffix assignment for each example. Primary sya, ḍha, ḍaṭ and āṭac still lack extension witnesses; the inherited local list even has short aṭac, plain dental tva, nik and other edition-specific readings.

independent_nominal_account: Three new heads are declined. No count for petva or lūni, whose written case forms already occur in PG190; the new contextual readings are separately retained. Neither pyātvam nor adverbial bhṛśam is projected into a full three-gender paradigm.
